related_resources.reason: Open Music Theory 2nd ed. II Counterpoint and Galant Schemas, section High Baroque Fugal Exposition. Direct locators: Basic Definitions; Structure / Voice Entries; Subject; Answer; Countersubject; Free Counterpoint; Links; Example (BWV 847 mm. 1-9). Author Mark Gotham credited on chapter. Source for period-specific terminology, not the original note events of this lecture.

Section 30.8 and Figures 30.8.1–30.8.4, BWV 847. Definitions of subject, answers, exposition/episode, bridge, two regular countersubjects, additional free counterpoint, subject-head fragmentation; distinguish from the original Bach source.

Terminology list and Fugues—Sample Questions; includes real and tonal answers, invertible counterpoint, episode, stretto, double fugue, canon; pedagogical conventions, not a claim that every fugue contains every device.

Distinct linked sections Invertible Counterpoint (Discussion and examples) and Fugue (Subject and Answer, Exposition and model fugues). Useful for pedagogy and planning, not an empirical validation of this original score.

Movement list for 24 prelude-fugue pairs; includes Prelude and Fugue in C minor BWV 847 and links to manuscript sources/editions. Historical score attribution separate from modern analyses and recordings; no score copied into this pack.

CUNY Graduate Center dissertation landing page; Abstract paragraphs on contrapuntal imitation and voice-leading patterns, 43 non-modulating subjects, three primary paradigms; do not assert detailed results beyond visible abstract.
Music Theory Spectrum 13(2) (Fall 1991), pp. 197–218. Abstract describes subject paradigms, linear progressions and recurring expositions. No specific uninspected passages or formulae asserted.

Exposition and real/tonal answer definitions visible in indexed search extract; direct full page inaccessible (403) in this pass. Use Gotham/Hutchinson as inspectable corroboration for detailed claims.
